learned_rules:
- **The money shape rates 8, or 9 if the radar shows the story still climbing and mcap is under ~$1M.** It looks like this: a MIGRATED coin leading on 5m volume, 25–45% off its local high, a printed higher low above the hourly low, 5m flow at or above the hourly pace, more buys than sells, top 10 under 15%, low RugCheck bundles. Both real winners looked like this (CATBOT 4.44x, FLOATER 2.19x, both under $1M) (V1, V6, V13). Rate it what it earns so code sizes it up (owner goal).
- **Owner floor: 7 under ~$1M mcap.** If the hard lines pass, flow is live (5m ≥ $10k and at or above pace), a higher low is printed and the first resistance is ≥1.5x away, rate it 7 or higher. Don't dock points for things the checklist already measured.
- **The MIGRATED buy zone is 10–60% off the local high** (owner rule). Within 10% of the high is a PASS, blocker "chasing" (42 skips: 3 ran, 36 dumped).
- **The shallow band (10–25% off the high) is a breakout trade, capped at 7.** It must be the 5m volume leader, pushing into the high right now, with flow at or above pace. Otherwise PASS, blocker "no breakout".
- **A spike counts as chasing anywhere in the zone.** If the last 5m candle is up more than 25% or 5m volume is more than 3x the hourly pace, wait for a retrace and a printed higher low. Blocker "chasing spike" (PILLSEY).
- **On MIGRATED, flow below pace or no printed higher low is a PASS, never a probe.** A printed higher low means three things: a bounce off the hourly low, a pullback that holds above it, and price back above that bounce's high. A buy share, a fib touch or a first green candle is not one. Blockers "flow below pace" / "no higher low" (Slingoor, ANAKIN, BLUE, SI, AAPLCAT never got past 1.01x).
- **Buy close to the structure.** Enter only within ~12% above the printed higher low, so the thesis breaks before the hard stop. Further above it is a mid-range entry: wait for a pullback or PASS, blocker "mid-range". Stops fill around −30 to −38%, not −20%, so entry distance is the real risk control.
- **Rate on the first resistance (prior high, POC or 0.618).** At ≥1.5x away it can rate 8–9. At 1.3–1.5x the cap is 7. Under 1.3x is a PASS, blocker "target too close" (PAWCAT, SWAN).
- **Above ~$1M mcap, a probe (6) is the most you take.** Only take it if the first resistance is ≥1.5x away and a breakout with flow at or above pace is printing right now. Otherwise PASS, blocker "big cap, no room" (1 green in 10).
- **A migration under 1h old that is still bleeding off its bond spike waits for a base above the hourly low.** Blocker "too new" (50 skips: 9 ran, 41 dumped).
- **In a vamp field, buy only the leader by 5m volume and radar mentions.** A bundle cluster inside a big same-ticker field is a PASS, blocker "split crowd" (V1, V3).
- **A DIP needs all of these:** a 40–70% drawdown, 5m flow at least 0.7x the hourly pace (owner gate, no "rising" needed), the story still on the radar, and a printed higher low with entry within ~12% of it. If all pass, size by conviction (7–8 when clean). A DIP whose catalyst already printed (news, rebrand) is a probe (6) at most until it reclaims its pullback high. A thin tech/LARP story is a PASS, blocker "dead story" (HEXN x2, SIS; DIPs 0 for 5).
- **Hard blocks:** top 10 over 25%, dev over 1%, bundles or insiders over the line, mint or freeze authority live, LP not burned, a political figure, RugCheck danger, any hack/exploit/drain story (V6, V13, V17, owner). Name the blocker in every PASS.
- **If RugCheck didn't load, it's a probe at most (6), not a block.** That needs the dossier's top-10 and dev numbers clean, mcap under $1M and the rest in the money shape. Say bundles are unverified.
- **Manage the trade; stops sell with no review.** If the printed higher low breaks, sell. If it hasn't reached 1.05x by minute 10 with flow under pace, exit. If it's green before initials and 5m volume drops under half the hourly pace, sell half. At the time stop, exit; the only extension is one 15-minute window while a volume surge at or above pace is printing. Re-enter a stopped-out coin only once, and only when it reclaims its prior high with flow at or above pace (re-entries 0 for 4).

daily_reviews.summary: No. After costs, every bucket loses money. Across 355 settled coins the simple plan (sell at 1.5x or -20%) averaged -10.1%, and before costs it was only about +0.4%. So the 10.5% round-trip cost on a $10 buy is the whole loss, and no group gets close to clearing it. The best group is MIGRATED at -8.1% net (about +2.3% before costs). With ~355 samples the all-coin result is clearly below zero, about -10% ± 3%. But the samples overlap: the same coin gets logged more than once, a few metas cluster, and it's all one market day. So the real uncertainty is wider, and a single day can't show any subgroup edge. The question about would-buys can't be answered: the routine model made zero BUY calls (would_buy n=0) and said PASS on all 181 coins it reviewed. Those passed coins ran more often than the checklist rejects (30.4% vs 16.1%) and lost less (-7.2% vs -13.1% net). That says the checklist filters somewhat, but nothing here is buyable.
findings: Costs are the whole story. All coins (n=355): 23.4% ran, 59.2% dumped, median peak 1.25x, 18.0% hit 2x. Before costs about +0.4%; after the 10.5% cost, -10.1%. A typical coin that peaks at 1.25x can't pay a 10.5% round trip.
MIGRATED is the least bad setup (n=250): 24.8% ran, 53.6% dumped, -8.1% net (about +2.3% before costs). It's the only setup positive before costs, and the margin is small enough to be noise.

DIP is clearly the worst (n=51): only 11.8% ran (6 coins), 72.5% dumped, 5.9% hit 2x, -18.4% net and about -8% even before costs. Its run rate is roughly half of MIGRATED's 24.8% on 250. With this gap it's unlikely to be just noise, though it's still only one day of data. Dip-buying as currently defined catches falling knives.

FINAL_STRETCH (n=54) has the biggest upside and still loses: median peak 1.45x, 27.8% hit 2x, but 72.2% dumped and -11.5% net. Ran plus dumped is exactly 100% and 'ran' equals 'hit 2x' exactly (27.8%), which looks like an artifact, not a real pattern (see data issues).

The checklist separates a little. Rejects (n=174): 16.1% ran, -13.1% net, about -2.8% before costs. Coins it let through to the model (n=181, all declined): 30.4% ran, -7.2% net, about +3.4% before costs. Dump rates are about the same (57.5% vs 60.8%), so the checklist finds more runners but doesn't avoid dumps.

Blocks that look worth keeping (48h, 'ran' share vs a ~23% baseline): bundles over the line 1/19 ran, and 3 of the 13 dumps went to 0.01–0.02x (rugs). Falling knife (code) 2/23. No higher low 1/15, with two Slingoor copies at 0.02x. Near the high / chasing 5/41 (12%). Political figure 0/3, holders/bundles unverified 0/3, hack story 0/2. The last three are tiny samples, but they all point the same way.

Blocks that don't seem to filter: too new 14/67 (21%), flow below pace 11/50 (22%), thin 5m volume 3/13 (23%). Their run rates match the ~23% baseline. But the baseline loses money, so loosening them would only add more losing trades. This is not a reason to loosen.
Top 10 over 25% (10/65 ran, 15%) and RugCheck danger (4/29, 14%) run less than the baseline. They're doing their job, even though GODHOUSE (3.19x) got through the top-10 rule's sample.

Real runners the model passed on: GIMODELO (MIGRATED, $103k mcap, 0.43h old) peaked at 7.45x. But it hit that at 352 of 360 minutes, too late for any 6h plan to bank most of it. CHICKPOT (DIP, $436k) did 10.5x after failing the checklist. Two big misses in a day don't change the averages.
Model capacity wasn't the bottleneck: 473 calls in 48h, 1 plan-limit hit, 7 candidates skipped with no model call, 0 stop reviews without the model.
rule_ideas: Cost gate: add the condition est_round_trip_cost_pct ≤ 5 and re-run every setup on the week's data. With costs at ~10.5%, a cost filter is the only lever big enough to matter. If the low-cost subset is still negative, the setups have no edge.

Drop or rebuild DIP: test setup=DIP only when drawdown_from_high is between 40% and 55%, 5m volume ≥ the 1h average pace (flow ratio ≥ 1.0), buy ratio ≥ 0.55, and the previous high was ≥ $150k mcap. If that subset doesn't beat -5% net on n≥40, turn DIP off.

MIGRATED focus: test setup=MIGRATED AND checklist passed AND mcap between $40k and $300k AND age between 0.5h and 6h AND 5m volume ≥ $10k AND buy ratio ≥ 0.55. Also split by mcap band to see whether the small positive before costs is concentrated anywhere.

FINAL_STRETCH exit variant: once the bonding-curve price switch is confirmed not to cause fake 2x hits, test selling half at 2x and trailing the rest (or a -30% stop), against the current all-out at 1.5x / -20%. 27.8% hit 2x, but the 1.5x target caps them while 72% eat the full stop.

Agreement signal: test whether coins where the checklist passed AND the model's conviction was ≥ 6 (even when it said PASS) beat the other checklist passes. To do this the model must log a conviction score on every PASS, not just a verdict.

Keep, don't loosen: bundles over the line, falling knife (code and no-higher-low), near the high / chasing, RugCheck danger, political figure, hack story. Re-check after the week; any block with a run rate under 15% and n ≥ 20 stays.

Hold-out test for too new / flow below pace: put coins blocked only by one of these two rules (everything else clean) through the same simulator. Loosen only if that subset beats the passed set's after-cost net by ≥ 5 points on n ≥ 30. That's unlikely given today's ~21–22% run rates.
data_issues: PUMP (Hxqh7…Ypump) is logged twice as a 332x and a 318x runner from ~$43–46k mcap. The same coin address also shows up in the 'crowd leaving' skips with best 1.0x and worst 0.24x. These can't all be true. The price feed is probably matching the wrong pool or the big PUMP token (pump.fun's own token, same ticker), or there's a decimals/units bug. Drop it from the top-runner list until fixed, and check the price source matches on coin address, not ticker.
FEAR (CHtX…pump) at 125.22x in the 'other' skips is also suspect. Several other FEAR coins in the same window dumped (one to 0.02x). Check the same thing: pool and coin-address match.

The 1.5x target caps the simulated gains, so these outliers barely move avg_net. But they do skew max_x and any future 'let the runner run' test. Cap or drop multiples above about 50x until each one is checked by hand.

would_buy n=0 across 181 model reviews. Either the model is far too strict or the watch-only setup is causing it. Check that the per-coin prompt doesn't tell the model trading is paused, because that would push every verdict to PASS. Also log the conviction score on every PASS. Without would-buys this week can't test the model at all.

FINAL_STRETCH has ran 27.8% + dumped 72.2% = 100% with zero flat, and hit_2x equals ran exactly. That points to a price jump when a coin moves from the bonding curve to the pool (different price source or units at migration), not real 2x moves. Check a few FS coins by hand.

Duplicates: the same coin address is logged more than once (PUMP twice in top runners; ZERO under both 'flow below pace' and 'other'; Marutaro under both 'too new' and 'price moved while deciding'). Samples aren't independent and skip counts double-count. Dedupe to the first entry per coin address per 6h, or report unique coins next to entry counts.

Window mismatch: the settled stats cover 24h but the skip tables cover 48h. 'ran' and 'dumped' in the skip tables don't say whether the coin hit 1.5x before or after -20%. Several 'ran' examples went below 0.85x first, so they're not wins under the simple plan. Report simple-plan net per block, not just ran/dumped counts.

Stop fills on rugs: several coins went to 0.01–0.03x. Confirm the simple plan fills those at the next sampled price, not at -20%; filling at -20% would understate losses. Also log the sampling interval.

Cost model: the 10.5% average on a $10 buy is probably mostly fixed costs. Check whether it counts refundable token-account rent as a cost, and report net at $10, $20 and $30 sizes. The conclusion depends heavily on this number.

No breakdown of setup by stage (e.g. MIGRATED by checklist result vs model review). The rules above can't be tested from the summary alone. Add it, and log 5m volume, flow ratio, buy ratio, drawdown, mcap and age on every row.

6h window cutoff: GIMODELO and SARAH hit their highs at 352–360 of 360 minutes, so max_x is cut off for coins still rising at the end. That's fine for the simple plan, but keep it in mind when quoting runner multiples.

daily_reviews.summary: Nothing has a positive edge after costs yet. All 359 settled coins averaged -10.2% net on the simple plan. Before costs that is about +0.4%, so the round-trip cost on a $10 buy (10.6% on average) accounts for the entire loss, the same story as the 22 real trades. FINAL_STRETCH comes closest: about +5.9% before costs, -5.1% after (n=46). At this sample size that is roughly one standard error from zero, from a single day's market, so it is noise until the full week says otherwise. I can't say whether the routine model's would-buys beat its passes, because it made zero would-buys out of 217 decisions. The coins it passed on averaged -11.2% net, the coins that failed the checklist -8.7%, and that gap is also noise.
findings: Costs decide everything. Average round-trip cost is 10.6% at $10 size. Before costs: all coins +0.4%, MIGRATED about -1.9%, DIP about +5.3%, FINAL_STRETCH about +5.9%. With the 1.5x / -20% plan, ignoring flat outcomes, a coin needs to hit 1.5x first about 44% of the time just to break even after 10.6% cost. No setup gets there (best is 37%).

FINAL_STRETCH (n=46): 37.0% hit 1.5x first, 63.0% hit the stop, median peak 1.54x, 39.1% touched 2x, net -5.1%. Over half of these coins peaked at 1.54x or more, yet only 37% reached 1.5x before -20%. Most of them shake out hard before moving, which fits the pre-bond dump in V1. Before costs: 0.37×50 − 0.63×20 = +5.9%, which matches the logged net once 11% cost is taken off.

MIGRATED (n=252, 70% of the sample) is the worst bucket: 20.2% ran, 61.1% dumped, median peak 1.22x, 13.5% touched 2x, net -12.4%. It loses even before costs (about -1.9%), so most of the day's sample is negative-expectancy coins.

DIP (n=61): 24.6% ran, 50.8% dumped (the lowest dump rate), net -5.2%. Only 4.9% touched 2x. Dips drift and rarely run, so on this data the 'let the runner run' idea has almost no tail to ride here. About +5.3% before costs, with a lot of it from coins that ended flat rather than from 1.5x exits.

Checklist vs model: coins that failed the checklist (n=142) ran 25.4% and netted -8.7%. Coins the model passed on (n=217) ran 21.7% and netted -11.2%. The soft parts of the filter are not separating winners from losers on this data.

Some skip reasons are clearly earning their keep (48h counts, before removing duplicates). Dev over 1%: 18 blocked, 0 ran, 14 dumped. Bundles over the line: 17 blocked, 0 ran, 13 dumped. Political figure: 4 blocked, 4 dumped. Holders/bundles unverified: 4 blocked, 0 ran. Too new: 64 blocked, 14% ran, 81% dumped. Falling knife (code): 23 blocked, 13% ran, 78% dumped. Top 10 over 25%: 63 blocked, 17% ran, 76% dumped. All of these sit at or below the 23% base run rate.

Some skip reasons look uninformative on small samples. RugCheck danger: 31 blocked, 26% ran, 68% dumped, roughly the base rate. Thin 5m volume: 17 blocked, 29% ran, 53% dumped. Neither is evidence for loosening anything. The 'thin' bucket probably mixes the hard <$2k line with softer cutoffs.
Near the high / chasing: 40 blocked, 20% ran, 70% dumped, and some went close to zero (PIRATE 0.01x, JIFFPOM 0.02x). Keep it.

The top runners are survivorship by construction. george (11.3x in 18 min), ZELDA (11.0x), Look (10.6x) and GTA (11.0x) were all brain PASS, and ABTC (23.3x) failed the checklist at 2.8 minutes old. That is 4-5 coins out of 359, and the simple plan caps every win at 1.5x anyway. Treat them as cases to review, not evidence that the model is too strict. Three of them were FINAL_STRETCH coins at 32-35k market cap, right around the ~34.6k bond level.
Model pacing is fine: 531 calls in 48h, 0 plan-limit hits, 0 candidates skipped for lack of a model call, 0 stop reviews without the model. No reason to change the pace.
rule_ideas: Cost gate: only consider coins whose estimated round-trip cost is at most 5%. First break net% down by cost bucket (<5%, 5-10%, >10%) and by buy size ($10 / $25 / $50). If most of the cost is fixed (priority fee, account rent), size matters more than coin selection. Any bigger size still has to fit the conviction risk budget.

FINAL_STRETCH with a clean checklist (no hard-line or soft fails) and 5m volume ≥ $10k (V1). Report n, share that ran, before-cost and after-cost net. Only adopt it if after-cost net is above zero with n ≥ 150 over the week.
FINAL_STRETCH with mcap ≥ 85% of the bond estimate vs below that. Tests whether the edge is concentrated right at bond. Beware: the runners were picked after the fact.

Exit variant for FINAL_STRETCH only: stop at -30% vs -20%, with the target at 1.5x and also tried at 2x. Check that the gain shows up in both halves of the week (Nov 3-6 vs Nov 7-10) before trusting it. Don't tune on a single day.

MIGRATED limited to the V6 range (mcap $70k-$11M) AND 5m volume ≥ $10k AND buy ratio ≥ 0.55 AND flow ratio (5m vs hourly pace) ≥ 1.0. If no subset beats costs on the week's data, turn MIGRATED off rather than tuning it.

DIP split by drawdown (40-55% vs 55-70% from the high) AND flow ratio ≥ 1.0 AND buy ratio ≥ 0.55. It has the lowest dump rate (50.8%), so check whether a smaller target (1.3x) with a -15% stop beats costs. Treat that as a high overfitting risk.

Check the model itself: among checklist-passing coins, compare the model's conviction scores (if logged) against outcomes. If the model never says BUY, have it log a 1-10 score on every pass so a 'score ≥ 6' rule can be tested.
Keep dev >1%, bundles, top 10 >25%, too new, political figure and falling knife (code) unchanged. The blocked coins under each of these dump at 76-100%.
data_issues: There were zero would-buys in 24h out of 217 model decisions. Check whether the watch-only instruction is leaking into the model's prompt and suppressing BUY verdicts, or whether would-buys aren't being logged. Either way, the main Nov 10 test (model picks vs passes) currently has no data. Fix this first.

Definitions don't line up. FINAL_STRETCH shows 39.1% touching 2x but only 37.0% 'ran', so 'ran' must mean 'hit 1.5x before -20%'. The skip buckets, though, call best_x ≥ 1.5 'ran' regardless of order (e.g. GTAVI 2.31x with a 0.87x low). Use one definition everywhere, and report simple-plan net% for the skip buckets too.

The skip buckets overlap and probably double-count. DESSA appears in four buckets, MEOWNERO in three, ORBIE and HI in two. The bucket totals add up to 382. Remove duplicates by contract address (first sighting) and give each coin one main reason, or every per-rule count is inflated.
The windows don't match: stats cover 24h, skips cover 48h. Compare on the same window.

Possible price-source jumps at migration. The top runners sat at 32-35k (bond level), with george at 11x in 18 minutes and ABTC at 23x. Check whether tracked prices switch from the pump.fun curve to the PumpSwap/Raydium pool, or to a different pair, partway through. Check the top max_x values against candle data.
Setup labels may be stale. george is labeled FINAL_STRETCH at $35.2k, above the ~$34.6k bond. ABTC is labeled MIGRATED at 2.8 minutes old. Log the bonding-curve % and the migration time.

The sampling interval isn't reported. The rule that counts a loss when both 1.5x and -20% were crossed between samples hurts volatile FINAL_STRETCH coins most. Log the interval and how often that tie happened.
Check how rugs settle. If liquidity is pulled and the price feed stops, does the coin settle near zero or at its last good price? The latter would make the results look better than they were.
The cost breakdown is missing. Log fixed vs size-proportional cost (platform fee, priority/bribe, slippage) so net% can be recomputed at other buy sizes.

The political filter seems to match on the coin's name or theme (Pooliticians, Groyper), while the hard line in V13 is about a politician posting the CA. Political-themed coins like TrumpWars, DJT, Impeach and POLITICATS went through other buckets. Log which signal fired.

daily_reviews.summary: This window has no evidence in it. In 24 hours zero coins were logged at any stage: none failed the checklist, none were passed by the brain, none were would-buys and none went unresearched. Nothing settled, nothing is still being followed, and the brain was called once in 48 hours. With n=0, nobody can say anything about an after-cost edge, and the question of whether the routine model's would-buys beat the coins it passed on has no data to answer. The only real finding is that the pipeline looks stalled. A scanner running around the clock should pass at least a handful of coins through the market filters every day. It's also Nov 14, four days after the planned Nov 10 test, so it's worth confirming the watch-only week was captured and archived before anyone talks about edge.
findings: Every stage has n=0 in the last 24 hours: checklist_failed, brain_passed, would_buy and not_researched. There is no share that ran and no net % to report.
No coins settled and none are still being followed, so the 6-hour price tracking has nothing to grade.
skips_48h is empty and top_runners is empty, so there's no record of passed coins running either. You can't tell whether a rule cost us anything.

The brain made 1 call in 48 hours with 0 plan-limit hits, 0 candidates skipped for lack of a brain and 0 stop reviews without a brain. The usage cap isn't the bottleneck. Too few candidates are reaching the brain at all.

Cost context from before the pause: 22 trades lost $25.79, and fees plus slippage were $18.83 of that (73%). Fees alone, not bad picks, were most of the loss. Any rule tested later has to clear that cost first.

Break-even math for the simple plan (sell at 1.5x or -20%): if the round trip on a $10 buy costs about 8% (roughly $0.86 a trade, the $18.83 average across 22 trades, assuming ~$10 positions), a win nets about +42% and a loss about -28%. The 1.5x has to be hit before -20% on more than about 40% of trades just to break even. That's the bar for the Nov 10 test.
rule_ideas: These come from the guide and from the cost math, not from this window, which has no data. Test them on the full archived Nov 3–10 week only, and require n≥30 per group before believing a net % number.

Cost gate: skip the coin if the estimated round-trip cost for a $10 buy on its pool is above about 4%. Test whether coins with lower costs have a positive net_pct under the simple plan while the rest don't. Fees were 73% of the past loss.
Volume floor: setup=MIGRATED or FINAL_STRETCH and 5m volume ≥ $10k (V1, V6, V13). Compare against $2k–$10k. A small difference in net % after costs means the bar isn't earning its keep.
Flow quality: buy ratio ≥ 0.55 and a flow ratio that shows 5m volume at or above its 1h pace. Check whether this separates coins that hit 1.5x from coins that hit -20% first.
DIP setup: drawdown from the recent high between 40% and 55%, versus 55% to 70%, both with 5m volume ≥ $10k. This tests the house rule that a 70% dip is still buyable against the falling-knife cases.

Market cap band: MIGRATED setup with mcap between $70k and $11M (V6), versus $30k to $70k (the V1 Dex tab range). Lower caps should have worse pool costs, so check whether the extra volatility pays for them.
Age: MIGRATED setup with age ≤ 2h versus 2h to 12h. Look for whether early migrated coins have an edge that survives the pre-bond and post-bond dumps.

Brain value: compare brain=would_buy against brain=passed among coins that cleared the checklist. If the would-buys don't beat the passes on net % with n≥30 each, the routine model adds no signal and conviction scores shouldn't drive sizing.

Checklist audit: among coins with checklist=failed, measure how many reached 1.5x before -20% compared with coins that passed. Only loosen a failed line if its blocked coins clear the ~40% break-even rate on a real sample. Hard lines don't move regardless.
data_issues: Zero coins at every stage in 24 hours. For a scanner that runs around the clock, that almost certainly means the scanner, the market filter or the logger has stopped or broken. It doesn't mean the market was empty. Check the process, the data source (DexScreener/RugCheck rate limits or API changes), and whether the filter thresholds were changed.

The brain made 1 call in 48 hours, but nothing records which coin or what the call was for. If it was a candidate decision, that coin should show up in a stage. If it was a maintenance or study call, it should be labeled that way.
skips_48h is empty. That fits a dead pipeline but could also mean skip logging broke on its own. These two failures need separate health checks.

The date is Nov 14 and the watch-only week was meant to be evaluated around Nov 10. This report doesn't say whether the Nov 3–10 data exists, is complete, or has been analyzed. Confirm that before any rules are tuned.

There's no heartbeat field, such as the last scan time or the number of coins scanned before the filters. Without one, an empty market can't be told apart from a stopped bot. Add scans_run, raw_tokens_seen and last_log_ts to the daily summary.

The cost model behind net_pct (pool-based round trip for a $10 buy) isn't shown with its inputs. Log the estimated cost for each coin so it can be checked against the real $18.83 in fees on 22 trades from before the pause.
